
TOPOLOGY
  processes       2 — every long-lived process this run starts, snug included:
                    snug        this process — resolves the policy and supervises
                    bwrap       the sandbox itself, and the payload inside it
                  No stage, no PRIVILEGED ancestor namespace — but see pid
                  nesting below: snug does create an unprivileged one.
  netns owner     sandbox
  pid nesting     depth 2 — snug forks bwrap into an intermediate user AND pid
                  namespace of its own making, so bwrap is pid 1 THERE and the
                  sandbox's own pid namespace nests below it. A process left at
                  the intermediate level has no /proc entry inside the sandbox:
                  unaddressable, not merely unreadable.
                  The intermediate user namespace is UNPRIVILEGED: identity
                  uid/gid map, and no capabilities survive bwrap's exec into it.
                  Cost: one more of the kernel's 32 user-namespace nesting
                  levels, and this run needs at least 2 each of
                  /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces and max_pid_namespaces.
  subuid          none (no delegated range; nothing needs one yet)
  control         none — there is no stage to control.
